display.purpose: Hero card number: network throughput value, disks-overview aggregate stat.

headline.purpose: Topbar page title; in-ring metric percentage (CPU/RAM/temp).

body.purpose: Table cell values, server-card rows, general UI text.

label.purpose: Uppercase table column headers, sidebar version tag.

motion.name: ease-fast
motion.purpose: Background/color/border-color transitions on hover (topbar buttons, nav items).

motion.name: ease-sidebar-collapse
motion.purpose: Sidebar width transition when collapsing to the icon-only rail.

motion.name: ease-progress
motion.purpose: Ring stroke-dashoffset and bar-width transitions when a live value updates.

motion.name: pulse-online
motion.purpose: The one shadow-based motion exception: expanding/fading ring on the online server-status dot.

components.name: Topbar Icon Button
components.description: 36×36px icon-only action button in the topbar (e.g. settings, refresh).
components.css: .ds-topbar-button { font: inherit; cursor: pointer; display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); background: #111A2E; color: #98A2C3; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-topbar-button:hover, .ds-topbar-button:focus-visible { background: #1A2541; outline: none; }

components.name: Sidebar Nav Item (active)
components.description: Active sidebar navigation entry with the gradient wash and left accent bar.
components.css: .ds-nav-item { width: 100%; background: none; font: inherit; text-align: left; cursor: pointer; position: relative; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 12px; border-radius: 10px; border: 1px solid transparent; color: #64748B; font-weight: 500; transition: background 0.15s, color 0.15s, border-color 0.15s; } .ds-nav-item--active { color: #E2E8F0; background: linear-gradient(135deg, color-mix(in srgb, #06B6D4 18%, transparent), color-mix(in srgb, #0EA5E9 9%, transparent)); border-color: color-mix(in srgb, #06B6D4 35%, transparent); } .ds-nav-item--active::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: -12px; top: 8px; bottom: 8px; width: 3px; border-radius: 0 3px 3px 0; background: #06B6D4; } .ds-nav-icon { flex-shrink: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 18px; height: 18px; }

components.name: Summary Card
components.description: The canonical metric card shell — icon chip + title header, flat surface, 12px radius.
components.html: CPU
components.css: .ds-summary-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 16px; min-width: 0; min-height: 360px; padding: 20px; border-radius: 12px; border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); background: #111A2E; overflow: hidden; } .ds-summary-card__header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; } .ds-summary-card__icon { flex-shrink: 0; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 36px; height: 36px; border-radius: 9px; background: rgba(129,140,248,0.12); color: #06B6D4; } .ds-summary-card__title { font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; color: #E2E8F0; }

components.name: Process Row
components.description: Top Processes table row with categorical avatar, right-aligned numeric columns, monospace-free (Figtree body).
components.css: .ds-processes-table { width: 100%; border-collapse: collapse; } .ds-processes-table__row td { padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.08); font-size: 13px; color: #98A2C3; } .ds-processes-table__row:hover { background: #1A2541; } .ds-processes-table__name-cell { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; } .ds-process-avatar { flex-shrink: 0; width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: 8px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 700; color: #FFF; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-process-avatar--0 { background: color-mix(in srgb, rgb(91,141,239) 18%, transparent); color: rgb(91,141,239); } .ds-processes-table__cpu, .ds-processes-table__mem, .ds-processes-table__pid { text-align: right; }

components.name: Ring Chart
components.description: Signature circular progress gauge with centered value/unit/label, used for CPU/RAM/temperature.
components.html: <svg class="ds-ring-chart" viewBox="0 0 120 120" width="110" height="110"><circle class="ds-ring-chart__track" cx="60" cy="60" r="52" fill="none" stroke="rgba(255,255,255,0.08)" stroke-width="8"></circle><circle class="ds-ring-chart__progress" cx="60" cy="60" r="52" fill="none" stroke="#06B6D4" stroke-width="8" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-dasharray="326.7" stroke-dashoffset="120" transform="rotate(-90 60 60)"></circle><text x="60" y="56" text-anchor="middle" font-size="22" font-weight="700" fill="#E2E8F0">63</text><text x="60" y="74" text-anchor="middle" font-size="14" font-weight="600" fill="#98A2C3">%</text></svg>

narrative.overview:
TrueNAS Dashboard is the dark-first, always-legible console for a home server: rings, sparklines, tables, and status dots read like instrumented gauges on a control-room wall, not a marketing surface. The mood is modern and vibrant rather than austere — Signal Cyan and Amethyst Signal give the flat dark surfaces real color and life, but they stay disciplined: each hue is tied to a specific channel of data (CPU/primary signal in cyan, RAM/inbound network in amethyst, outbound network and healthy states in green), never used decoratively. Nothing here is illustrative or aspirational; every visual element maps to a real, live number.

The system is currently mid-migration: this DESIGN.md documents the new sidebar+topbar UI (index-updated.html / style-updated.css), which is where active development (including the new Top Process Panel) is happening. The legacy UI (index.html / style.css) is being retired in its favor per the project roadmap.
keyCharacteristics: Dark by default (html[data-theme="dark"]), with a fully-specified light theme as the alternate, not an afterthought.
Flat everywhere — depth comes from tonal layering (background → surface → surface-hover), not shadows.
One typeface (Figtree) for everything; hierarchy comes from size and weight, not font-mixing.
Inline stroke-SVG icons throughout (Lucide-style, 24×24 viewBox, 2px stroke, round caps) — no icon fonts, no image icons.
A tight, semantic set of state colors (success / warning / danger) applied consistently across disks, pools, and process rows.

rules.name: The Numeric Monospace Rule
rules.body: Disk names, temperatures, and percentages render in monospace, not Figtree — so columns of shifting numbers stay visually aligned instead of jittering as digit widths change.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Design Rule
rules.body: Never add a resting box-shadow to a card, button, or row. If a component needs to read as "raised," lighten it one tonal step (surface → surface-hover) or add a border, not a shadow.

dos: Do drive every color and every repeated spacing/radius value through a CSS custom property — never hardcode a hex or px value that duplicates an existing token.
Do build icons as inline stroke SVG (24×24 viewBox, 2px stroke, round linecap/linejoin) — matches every existing icon in the system.
Do use <button>, never <a>, for in-app navigation and controls (sidebar nav, topbar actions).
Do prefer flexbox for layout; reach for CSS grid only when flex genuinely can't express the layout.
Do use semantic class names that describe the entity (server-card-row, processes-table-row), never the layout shape (server-full-width).
Do keep Signal Cyan and Amethyst Signal tied to their specific data channels (primary/CPU and secondary/RAM+RX respectively) rather than using them interchangeably as generic accents.
donts: Don't add a resting box-shadow anywhere — the system is flat by rule; the pulse-ring on the online dot is the one motion exception, not a precedent for card elevation.
Don't put ApexCharts (or any chart library) on a summary card — native SVG only there; ApexCharts is reserved for the dedicated detail pages (cpu-apex.html and its siblings).
Don't build list markup with innerHTML; clone the existing <template> once and update only the values on refresh (disks, cores, pools, and process rows all follow this pattern).
Don't introduce a second font family or a decorative display face — Figtree carries the whole hierarchy by size/weight alone.
